item.title: Entrepreneurship and the Creation of Decent Work for All
item.content:encoded:
This multi-journal collection addresses the relationship between entrepreneurship and decent work, aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goal 8. The collection recognizes that recent disruptions have highlighted how rapidly employment situations can change, and that entrepreneurship may play a significant role in creating quality employment opportunities, particularly in volatile environments.

The collection seeks to bring together diverse research perspectives on how entrepreneurship can contribute to productive employment, fair wages, improved labor market access, and better job opportunities across different contexts and populations. Both research and review articles are welcome, and all submissions will undergo rigorous peer review according to each journal's standards.

Appel publié par Small Business Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Equal pay for work of equal value
  • Gender discrimination in employment
  • Immigration and employment
  • Labor shortages after COVID-19
  • Modern slavery and child labor
  • Labor policy
  • Entrepreneurial enterprises, SMEs, and family businesses
  • Global entrepreneurial firms: organization design, emerging conceptions in entrepreneurship (i.e. born globals), globalization's challenges and opportunities, cultural differences
  • Remote work
  • Opportunity entrepreneurship as a direct way to generate high quality employment
  • Measuring and dealing with positive and negative externalities of new businesses

item.title: Entrepreneurship, Creative Destruction, and Growth: Enriching the Aghion-Howitt Tradition
item.content:encoded:
Philippe Aghion, Collège de France

Martin Andersson, Blekinge Institute of Technology

David B. Audretsch, Indiana University

Maksim Belitski, University of Reading

Pontus Braunerhjelm, KTH Royal Institute of Technology

This special issue seeks to advance Schumpeterian research that integrates entrepreneurial activities across multiple levels of analysis. It focuses on connecting individual entrepreneurs and firms with regional innovation ecosystems and industrial dynamics, while also considering broader institutional and policy frameworks.

The issue welcomes research on the full lifecycle of ventures, including formation, growth, contraction, and failure, with particular emphasis on how these dynamics drive productivity improvements. It also invites studies that enrich the Aghion-Howitt growth model with contemporary entrepreneurship research insights.

Appel publié par Small Business Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • New venture formation and post-entry dynamics
  • Scaling, displacement, and exit in entrepreneurial firms
  • Reallocation dynamics and productivity growth
  • The Aghion-Howitt framework and entrepreneurship research
  • Multi-level analysis connecting micro (entrepreneurs and firms), meso (regional ecosystems and industrial structure), and macro (institutional configurations and policy regimes) levels
  • Innovation and its transformation into productivity growth within the Schumpeterian tradition

Timeline

  • November 1, 2026: Submission deadline
